newsitem.title: USA: CBOE considering Lipper-Salomon fund index options.
newsitem.headline: CBOE considering Lipper-Salomon fund index options.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) said it was considering listing options on mutual fund indexes.
"We are very interested in it," said Alger "Duke" Chapman, the outgoing CBOE chairman. He was in Tucson to attend a business conference on risk management.

Michael Lipper, president of Lipper Analytical Services, which tracks mutual fund performance, said his firm had been approached by Salomon Inc's Salomon Brothers unit last year with the idea of developing options on Lipper's fund indexes.
The firm used its existing growth fund index and growth and income fund index as the basis for the fund index options.
"It would be the Lipper Analytical-Salomon Brothers Growth Fund Index and then the Growth and Income Fund Index," he said in a telephone interview.
Salomon declined to comment. Chapman said the CBOE had been in talks with Lipper and Salomon on the possibility of listing mutual fund index options.
"We haven't filed with the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) for it, and we still have to have our board approve it," he said.
Lipper said the indexes had been designed in a "non-controversial" way, suggesting easy approval from the SEC, but added: "You never know with the commission."
He added that Salomon's participation in the project was key because the firm would be able to market the product to institutional investors.
"What I am hoping is that with Salomon's name attached, they will be continuously marketing to their markets," he said, adding that retail participation might eventually emerge.
Chapman called the idea "interesting" and noted that a record number of U.S. investors had been investing in securities through mutual funds and 401(k) savings programs.
"Obviously there are some customers who are interested in it," he said.
Lipper said he was curious to see how the options would fare if and when they are approved and launched.
"A lot of these things in theory work one way but in practice work another," he said.
